newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jordan says Jews could cause explosion in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Jordan says Jews could cause explosion in Hebron.

text.p: Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan said in an interview published on Friday that Jewish settlement inside Hebron could lead to an "explosion".

The prince also slammed slogans used by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during his May election campaign as cliches that were delaying a deal on implementing an Israeli troop withdrawal from most of the West Bank town.
"We've become victims of cliches," the prince was quoted by the Israeli daily Haaretz as saying. "Peace for peace, security for peace. These words have no meaning."

"There inside Hebron several dozen Jewish settlers, with their families, could create an explosion unless something deep, deeper than police or uniformed soldiers, will ensure they conduct their lives in coexistence with the surroundings," he added.

Israel-PLO talks on implementing the long-delayed withdrawal from Hebron have snagged on Israel's demand its troops be allowed to re-enter the 80 percent of Hebron slated to fall under PLO control if they are chasing suspected guerrillas.
Netanyahu opposes trading occupied Arab land for peace but has said he will uphold deals, like that on Hebron, signed by the Labour government he ousted in May elections.
He insists there must be added security guarantees for some 400 Jews who live and study amidst the 100,000 Palestinian residents of Hebron before he will implement the withdrawal.
Jordan and Israel signed a peace treaty in October 1994.

Prince Hassan in September postponed a visit to Israel because he had "overburdened schedules" but Israeli media said the trip was put off because Jordan feared being seen as the only Arab country in close contact with Israel.
